title: Traumatic Brain
Injury
Rehabilitation
hero.text: For patients recovering from traumatic brain injury, to restore physical, behavioural and cognitive function, leading to greater independence.

overview: A traumatic brain injury (TBI) occurs when a sudden impact, blow or jolt to the head disrupts normal brain function. Depending on the severity, a TBI can affect movement, cognition, behaviour, speech and emotional regulation. Symptoms may appear immediately or develop over time, ranging from headaches and confusion to significant physical, cognitive or behavioural changes.

topics.label: What Is Traumatic Brain Injury Rehabilitation?

blocks.text: Traumatic Brain Injury rehabilitation is specialised care for patients whose movement, cognition, behaviour, speech or daily function has been affected by a head injury. At Cambridge Hospital, our TBI rehabilitation programme supports recovery after mild, moderate and severe brain injuries caused by falls, accidents or other traumatic events.

Care is delivered by a coordinated, interdisciplinary team working within one structured pathway, combining medical management with physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech and language therapy and cognitive rehabilitation.
Each programme is built around personalised, measurable goals, helping patients regain independence, improve daily function and rebuild confidence.
Our rehabilitation programme addresses physical, cognitive and emotional recovery through a coordinated approach:

items: **Physiotherapy** - building strength, balance, flexibility and coordination
**Occupational therapy** - relearning daily activities such as feeding, dressing, bathing, using the toilet and moving safely
**Speech and language therapy** - supporting speech, language, cognition and safe swallowing
**Cognitive therapy** - improves memory, attention, judgment, planning, perception, thinking and learning
**Psychological counselling** - building coping skills, strengthening emotional wellbeing and rebuilding relationships

blocks.text: Rehabilitation is an important part of recovery for patients following traumatic brain injury. Once a patient is medically stable and ready to leave acute hospital care, the next stage of care depends on their individual medical, functional and rehabilitation needs.
Depending on the patient’s specific condition, there are two primary pathways for post-hospital care:

items: **Long-term care facilities:** For patients who are medically stable but continue to require ongoing medical support, nursing care or mechanical ventilation.
**Rehabilitation centres:** For patients who are medically stable and able to participate in rehabilitation but require support to regain physical, cognitive, communication or daily living skills.

blocks.text: The rehabilitation team assesses each patient’s needs and develops an individualised care plan, with the level and intensity of support adjusted as recovery progresses.
